dialogues.speaker: Gendou Ringo
dialogues.text: You want a fortune slip?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Geez, she's so cold.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes, I'd like one...

dialogues.speaker: Gendou Ringo
dialogues.text: Got it. Here's how it goes. First, shake this... thing over here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Isn't it called a Fortune Slip Box?

dialogues.speaker: Gendou Ringo
dialogues.text: Yes. A Bamboo Slip will drop out from it. Give it to me, and I'll give you a matching strip of paper.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm pretty sure they say it's a Fortune Slip...

dialogues.speaker: Gendou Ringo
dialogues.text: Whatever.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's got a question! If... What do we do if we get one that means bad luck?

dialogues.speaker: Gendou Ringo
dialogues.text: It's fate. You got a problem with that? Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Isn't there that shelf-like thing outside we can use to...

dialogues.speaker: Gendou Ringo
dialogues.text: Tsk.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did she seriously just say "tsk"?

dialogues.speaker: Gendou Ringo
dialogues.text: Let me see... Oh right, so it's like this. "Tie the inauspicious slip onto the Fortune Slip Hanger to change ill fortune to good"...

dialogues.speaker: Gendou Ringo
dialogues.text: Ah, right! If you get a slip with ill fortune, just tie it to that shelf, that'll do.

dialogues.speaker: Gendou Ringo
dialogues.text: Huh, what a bunch of... No, sorry. We at the Grand Narukami Shrine are most gentle indeed. Even if you should draw a slip with bad luck, you shall have a chance to turn it around.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Something about this doesn't seem right...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Let's go draw a slip, {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let Paimon see, let Paimon see.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! It says very auspicious. Yeah!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like today's Paimon's lucky day!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yours?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! Your fortune is Paimon's fortune! And vice versa, Paimon's fortune is also your fortune.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: When Paimon eats good food, that's good fortune. So, for the sake of your fortune, please give Paimon some good food.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let Paimon see, let Paimon see.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, not bad.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Being with Paimon will certainly bring you good fortune!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let Paimon see, let Paimon see.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh, it's inauspicious!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon remembers this scenario! It said... to "tie the inauspicious slip onto the Fortune Slip Hanger."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "And then treat Paimon to some good food. That will help change the bad luck into good!"

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is that so?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course! Are you questioning the wisdom of the ancients?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The wisdom of the ancients is incredible! Anyway, let's find the Fortune Slip Hanger first!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? What's this? Looks like someone's notes. Let Paimon see...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "... Shuumatsu... Fatui... plot against..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is this? It's a mess, and it's all covered in stains. Paimon can't really read it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could be a clue to some treasure.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That makes sense! Let Paimon have another look.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "... when deciphering the slip, the secret code... "

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let Paimon see! "...The first half is 'In the middle of a hazy night'... "

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It cuts off here, and Paimon can't tell what the second half is.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But since it used a secret code, there must be some kind of secret to be found, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Either way, this seems important. Next time we decipher our fortune slip, let's try to match the secret codes, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #(Hey, {NICKNAME}!)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (According to that Ms. Gendou, this Ms. Gendou is...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Yeah, a Fatui knockoff.)

dialogues.speaker: Gendou Ringo
dialogues.text: Ah, we meet again. Want to check your fortune as well? Or...

dialogues.speaker: Gendou Ringo
dialogues.text: If you need a listening ear or if you have something to discuss, I can help too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ms. Gendou is so friendly!

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: Is that so? Hehe, that's what many people have told me lately. It feels good.

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: It's always been my dream to work at a beautiful shrine like this.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (She is a Fatuus in disguise.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Hmm... but she's quite friendly...)

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: #So, {NICKNAME}, how may I help you today?

choices.text: I'm just here to see you.

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: Me... Huh? Ah? S—Sorry, I don't understand what you... what you mean...

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: P—Please allow me to cool down a little...

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: I get it now. Come find me if you have any questions.

choices.text: (Wait for Ms. Gendou to contact us.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Where did Ms. Gendou go?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, this is slightly distressing...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right? What if she doesn't return? How will Paimon know today's fortune?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? There's a slip here. Let Paimon have a look...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We shouldn't...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It doesn't matter! It could be a clue!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? This is...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems like we're to go to... this place and receive further instructions...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go find out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ms. Gendou's attitude is the same as ever, huh... Anyway, let's check the slip's contents.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? This is...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, Paimon gets it. This must refer to some bad guy who needs defeating!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, that's gotta be it. So, Ms. Gendou, you're a secret agent who's using this method to communicate and wipe out those who try to harm Inazuma, right?

dialogues.speaker: Gendou Ringo
dialogues.text: You talk too much.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Welp! S-sorry! Please don't sic the "Shuumatsu" on us!

dialogues.speaker: Gendou Ringo
dialogues.text: Leave now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're leaving right now! Let's go to the place shown in the picture and see if we can find our target!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is the place, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's nothing special here...
You showed up indeed, just as I expected.

dialogues.speaker: Gendou Ringo
dialogues.text: Who are you, exactly, and what are your intentions?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's our line! What were you doing, Ms. Gendou, attacking us like that?

dialogues.speaker: Gendou Ringo
dialogues.text: How rude. Answer my question.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #I'm {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Gendou Ringo
dialogues.text: Oh, I know your names, alright. Now, tell me. Where did you hear the secret code from?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, what are you saying!? Just tell Ms. Gendou what happened already! Can't you see the super scary look in her eyes?

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: I see. So you chanced upon those notes. In that case, Momoka must be...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Who's Momoka?

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: She was the one who penned those notes, and she was a colleague of mine. Unfortunately, she will no longer be able to continue serving Inazuma. A true shame...

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: I'm sure you must have many questions. I suppose it couldn't hurt to answer them.

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: Momoka and I are both ninja of the Shuumatsuban. Our task is to rid Inazuma of external threats, and these "strips of paper" are one of the ways in which we communicate our missions.

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: As a result, we have also endured a lot of resentment and peril. For example, from those dangerous people who have infiltrated our nation...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What do you mean Mondstadters!

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: We use secret codes to identify our comrades.

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: However, each person's secret code is unique. It seems that Momoka deliberately left her secret code behind in a bid to inform us of the situation.

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: ...She was attempting to lure the enemy who would want to use that secret code out.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you found out immediately, didn't you, Ms. Gendou?

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: Of course. That's why I had to ascertain the situation. But it truly was strange. I couldn't work it out.

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: If you really were Snezhnayan spies, then why would you go and complete the missions as ordered without reporting the matter back to the Fatui?

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: ...As such, I believe your story about the abandoned camp.

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: From your actions, I can see that while you only matched the secret code up out of curiosity at first, you are friends and not foes of Inazuma.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that's our name cleared — but Paimon's still a little peeved that you've just taken us for free labor this whole time, Ms. Gendou!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Was that person really you though?

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: Hmph, I see you've noticed. Yes, the Gendou who gave you missions afterwards is an impostor.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What?

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: As I was tailing you, I was set upon by some Fatui spies.

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: I do know a thing or two about ninja arts myself, so I faked my death to fool them.

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: Afterward, they simply had one of their own people disguise themselves as me and replace me.

choices.text: No wonder she felt so off.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? So does that mean that the kind-hearted Ms. Gendou was a fake?

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: "Kind-hearted"? Hmph, I suppose she's been quite popular, huh?

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: Well, either way, they must've assumed that you were a formal member of the Shuumatsuban, and tried to use you to infiltrate our organization.

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: This proved to be a good opportunity for me. While that impostor was out, I used methods of my own to bring you here.

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: Listen well. I shall now give you a choice.

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: Work for us as an external member. They do not yet know that I live, so the advantage is ours at present.

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: You could certainly try.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Whatever the case might be, {NICKNAME}, the Fatui are our enemies too! Why don't we work together?

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: A wise choice. The supplies in this safe house are yours to use as you please.

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: Well then. I will be in touch in the event that something new comes up.

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: May our cooperation be fruitful. Farewell.

choices.text: No wonder she called the Fortune Slip by its proper name.

response.speaker: Gendou Ringo
response.text: That's right.

choices.text: Please listen to me. This is how it happened...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We found an abandoned camp on a hill...

dialogues.speaker: Gendou Ringo
dialogues.text: Give me that bamboo slip.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: R—Right.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This shrine really seems to lack the whole divine affection thing, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Gendou Ringo
dialogues.text: Here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see how our luck's going...

dialogues.speaker: Gendou Ringo
dialogues.text: Ah, yes. You can only draw one fortune slip each day. Please remember that.

dialogues.speaker: Gendou Ringo
dialogues.text: It's too tiring otherwise... Wait, no. If not, you won't be able to use the Fortune Slip Hanger to... No, that's not right either. What was I supposed to say?

dialogues.speaker: Gendou Ringo
dialogues.text: "Fortune slips are the manifestation of our archon's will. It is our place as mortals to respect it and do all we can."

dialogues.speaker: Gendou Ringo
dialogues.text: See? Elegantly put. So please remember, you can only draw one fortune slip each day.
